trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.

Going up-left, the next 2 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at number 2; going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 2 (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-right.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes left.

Going up-left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (3,-3); going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-right.
Going left would leave number 4 unreachable without crossing a higher number. So the line goes up-right.
The line must go up-left: left is number 6, which comes later.
Going down-left would strand number 6: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going down-right would turn number 6 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going left, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down-left.

Number 7 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going left, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at number 9. So the line goes down-left.
Going down-left would force the line onto number 17 before its turn; going left would cut off the bottom edge (8 cells). So the line goes up-left.
Going left would cut off the bottom edge (9 cells); going down-left would cut off the bottom edge (8 cells). So the line goes up-left.
Going up-left would force the line onto number 16 before its turn; going down-left would leave both number 16 and cell (-3,2) needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes right.
The line must go up-right: up-left is number 15, which comes later.
Going left would leave both number 14 and number 15 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Going down-left would turn number 15 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes left.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
